title: Capacity Safety Net Operator and Edge Eviction Handbook (PRD draft)
content:
Purpose
This doc sketches a production-ready pattern for handling short-term demand spikes and long-term capacity pressure in Dedicated pools. The focus: a lightweight operator (Capacity Safety Net Operator, aka SNO) that orchestrates elastic headroom, isolation boundaries, and a graded eviction protocol so customer tenants see graceful degradation rather than hard failures.

Context / why now
- We ship more Dedicated capacity customers with burst requirements and mixed SLAs.
- Existing approaches either over-reserve (waste) or bluntly evict tenants under pressure, causing downstream outages and escalations.
- We need an operationally simple mechanism that: 1) preserves latency SLOs for high-priority tenants, 2) gives predictable, debuggable outcomes for mid/low tenants, 3) limits cost by using transient pools and rebalancing.

Goals
- Allow short bursts above committed capacity while bounding cost and latency tail impact.
- Provide tenant-level controls for soft degradation vs hard eviction (customer-configurable).
- Enable automated, observable decisioning with clear audit trails and rollbacks.
- Make runbook steps unambiguous for SRE and on-call.

Non-goals
- Not a full replacement for long-term capacity planning or billing model changes.
- Not intended to guarantee zero-cold-start for on-prem private deployments in air-gapped modes.

Definitions (quick)
- Headroom credit: a time-limited unit representing permission to exceed committed throughput (measured as GPU-seconds or token-rate weight).
- Warm pool: pre-initialized workers (or reserved GPU slices) that can be attached quickly to a tenant to reduce cold-start latency.
- Soft degrade: reduced fidelity (smaller model, quantized variant, batched higher concurrency) used to maintain throughput but potentially lower per-request quality.
- Hard eviction: forced termination or queueing of tenant requests until capacity is available.

High-level design: Capacity Safety Net Operator (SNO)
SNO responsibilities
- Maintain global headroom ledger across a pool (dedicated region/pool).
- Accept/deny burst requests based on policy, predicted tail risk, and current credits.
- Trigger warm pool attach/detach workflows and model variant fallbacks.
- Execute graded eviction and throttling when utilization crosses thresholds.
- Emit events to the Console and audit logs for every decision.

Core components
1) Headroom Engine
  - Inputs: real-time utilization, pending queue lengths, per-tenant SLO weight, historical burst patterns.
  - Outputs: grant/deny tokens, suggested warm pool size, recommended model variant.
  - Policy knobs: max-burst-per-tenant, global-burst-cap, decay-window (how fast credits drain).

2) Isolation Lattice
  - Tiers: protected, standard, opportunistic.
  - Protected = enterprise SLO (no soft degrade allowed except as last resort), Standard = allow soft degrade and short bursts, Opportunistic = preemptible, best-effort.
  - Mapping: tenant-level tag + SLA mapping from billing/console.

3) Eviction Gradient Engine
  - Phase 0 (green): < 70% baseline utilization. No action.
  - Phase 1 (caution): 70–85%. Recommend warm pool attach for increasing tenants, suggest soft degrade policies.
  - Phase 2 (squeeze): 85–95%. Enforce soft degrade for standard tenants, throttle opportunistic flows with controlled queueing.
  - Phase 3 (critical): >95%. Scoped hard eviction only on opportunistic tenants, surgical reclaim for cold/idle sessions, initiate cross-pool spillback if available.
  - Each transition creates a deterministic audit entry and a suggested rollback plan.

4) Warm Pool Orchestrator
  - Maintains a small, regional warm pool per hardware class. Warm pool sizing is driven by observed burst percentiles (P90 burst magnitude over last 7d).
  - Attach cost model: each attach consumes headroom credits and increments warm-pool billing attribution.

Signals and telemetry
- Required signals: GPU utilization per node, queue length per tenant route, 99/95/50 latency per tenant, KV cache hit rate, recent burst frequency, warm pool occupancy, headroom ledger state.
- Derived signals: burst velocity (tokens/sec delta), preemption risk score (0–100), tenant-health (combination of latency, error-rate, recent grants).

Decisioning heuristics (sketch)
- On incoming request surge: estimate sustained delta using 30s and 5m windows; if predicted sustained > burst threshold and tenant in protected tier -> consult SLO override (manual or policy auto-grant limited).
- If tenant in standard tier and predicted sustained < max-burst-per-tenant -> grant headroom for short-window, attach warm pool if attach latency < configured budget.
- If multiple tenants request concurrently and global-burst-cap would be exceeded -> apply proportional rationing by SLO weight, prefer shorter-lived bursts.

Billing and economics model (ops-aware)
- Headroom credits allocated monthly and can be purchased or earned via commit discounts.
- Active warm pool attachments bill at a per-attach rate + time-in-use.
- Eviction logs tie back to billing events so CS can explain customer-impact to accounts.

APIs and Console UX (surface area)
- Tenant-facing API: request_burst(tenant_id, estimate_peak, duration_hint) -> {granted: bool, credits_used, fallback_variant}.
- Admin Console: visual timeline of headroom churn, per-tenant risk score, and ability to pin/unpin warm pool attachments.
- Alerting: SNO emits priority events: GRANT_DENIED, SOFT_DEGRADE_STARTED, HARD_EVICTION_EXECUTED. All events include causal chain and recommended remediation.

Operational runbook (abridged)
- OnGRAY (Phase 1->2 transition): notify #dedicated-capacity, auto-scale warm pool by +1 per hot-tenant, set temporary 5-minute override to soft-degrade for opportunistic.
- OnRED (Phase 2->3): page on-call, suspend opportunistic traffic with pre-announced window, begin cross-pool spillback if configured.
- Post-incident: run headroom ledger audit (JIRA OPS-3172) and create customer-impact ticket for any protected tenant affected.

Rollout plan (phases)
- Experiment (2 months): SNO in observation mode (decisions logged but not enforced) on 1 non-prod pool. Metrics: decision-stability, false-positive degrade rate, attach latency distribution.
- Canary (1 month): Enforce soft-degrade and warm pool attach for standard tier on two small production pools. Manual gate for hard eviction is retained.
- Broad rollout (ongoing): Enable full policy; hard eviction autopilot after maturity thresholds met (safety: <1% customer-impact for protected tenants).

Success metrics
- Reduce customer-visible hard-eviction incidents by 80% in 90 days.
- Maintain 99th percentile latency SLO for protected tier with <5% extra cost from warm-pool attaches.
- Headroom spend efficiency: median credits consumed per burst episode decreases vs naive over-provision baseline.

Security and compliance considerations
- Ensure audit logs for every SNO decision are tamper-evident and routed to the existing audit KMS pipeline.
- Customer opt-in: enterprise customers can require explicit manual approvals for any degradation action.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How aggressive should decay be for headroom credits? (short decay favors fairness but increases churn).
- Warm pool sizing: centralized across region vs per-pool—trade memory/cost vs attach latency.
- Billing UX: should opportunistic attaches be surfaced as credits or invoice line items?

Next steps (concrete)
1) Engineering spike: implement mock SNO that consumes real-time metrics and emits decisions to a local stream (2 weeks) — owner: Miguel.
2) Telemetry backlog: add derived signals (burst velocity, preemption risk score) to pool metrics (1 sprint) — owner: Priya.
3) Runbook draft: SRE to author detailed steps for Phase 2->3 transitions with rollback commands (1 week) — owner: Ben.
4) Console prototyping: simple timeline view + emergency pin toggle (design + prod prototype, 3 weeks) — owner: Laura.

Appendix: quick sample incident sequence (narrative)
- 14:03 pool utilization spikes from ad-hoc tenant A due to model retrain traffic. SNO observes predicted sustained delta and grants a 90s headroom token (tenant A standard tier).
- 14:04 warm pool attach starts (attach latency 1.2s), requests rerouted to attached workers; latency recovers but headroom ledger shows rapid drain.
- 14:06 another tenant B also bursts; SNO applies proportional rationing; tenant B's requests see soft degrade (smaller variant) while A continues.
- 14:08 global utilization hits 92%: SNO flips Phase 2 policy; opportunistic tenants are throttled to 50% while protected tenants maintain throughput. Audit trail stored and Ops alerted.
- Post incident: ledger reconciled and billing events created; CS notified if protected tenant experienced any quality reduction.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally a working doc: please flag unclear failure modes, missing telemetry, or painful operator steps.
- If you have customer scenarios (names/ids) we should simulate in the spike, drop them in JIRA:DED-8421.
